title: Introduce ephemeral tenant-scoped keys and audit entropy aggregator
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customer audits and internal threat modeling highlighted two gaps: long-lived tenant keys increasing blast radius for operator compromise, and noisy audit streams that make user-level action correlation and deduplication expensive. This PR introduces two coordinated capabilities: 1) ephemeral tenant-scoped CMK wrapping (tenant-scoped ephemeral DEKs provisioned and rotated per-lease) and 2) an audit entropy aggregator that canonicalizes audit metadata and computes a compact entropy fingerprint to help downstream dedupe, sampling, and privacy-preserving indexing. Goals: minimize long-tail key exposure, provide a migration path for existing tenants, and reduce downstream audit volume while preserving provable non-repudiation. High level changes: - KMS subsystem: add tenant-scoped ephemeral key manager with lease TTLs, renewal logic, and fallbacks to tenant CMKs when configured. - Authz: RBACv2 hook extended to attach tenant lease claims to operator tokens; new policy predicate to require ephemeral lease for high-risk operations. - Audit pipeline: new aggregator service that computes an entropy fingerprint (sha256-based canonicalizer + salt per-tenant), supports rewrite rules for PII markers, and emits compact audit records to the main audit store. - Runtime: integration with request router to attach key provenance headers and to annotate traces. Backwards compatibility: feature gated by operator flags (feature.ephemeral-tenant-keys, feature/audit-entropy-agg) and default-off. Migration: opt-in per-tenant through Console or API; a rolling migration tool included (migration/ephemeral-key-adopter) that swaps token-binding for routes. Security considerations: TTL defaults to 12h for tenant DEKs, operator scopes cannot request leases longer than tenant policy allows. Checklist: - [x] KMS manager implementation + unit tests - [x] RBAC predicate + policy changes + unit tests - [x] Audit aggregator + integration tests - [x] Console API + docs updated - [x] E2E run in staging and perf baseline measured - [x] Feature flags and rollout playbook added Rollout plan: Stage behind feature flags; enable for internal tenants first, run audit-aggregator in parallel with current pipeline for 2 weeks, validate entropy collision rate and perf impact, then opt individual customers in. Risks and mitigations: potential increase in KMS calls -> added local caching and prefetch; audit aggregator may increase CPU load -> autoscale policy added. See linked linear tasks for acceptance criteria and perf SLOs.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Flagged potential high QPS to KMS during rush traffic; asked for caching numbers and benchmarks. Response: added prefetch + batched Encrypt operations, included load test section in perf results.

Rina Sato: Asked for clarification on audit fingerprint salt rotation and storage. Response: salt is per-tenant, rotated on a 90-day schedule, and stored encrypted with tenant CMK; rotation triggers re-hash of incoming events only (no retroactive rewrite).

Samir Patel: Requested that lease TTL be configurable per-tenant and bounded by policy. Response: implemented tenant.metadata.max_lease_ttl and validation in lease_store, plus Console UI to surface limits.

Rina Sato: Security review requested adding a KMS usage quota metric and alert. Response: added ephemeral_kms_calls_total and an alert in deploy/charts/alerts.yaml; CI checks updated to include the alert rule linting.

notes: This PR intentionally keeps tenant lease default conservative (12h) to limit blast radius; security team to review TTLs after initial rollout. The audit fingerprint size is configurable; default uses 8 bytes (base64) to balance collision risk and storage.
